scene:L1.01:0.text: Sam woke up to a loud bang. It was not thunder — it was the neighbor fixing his old truck again!
scene:L1.01:0.draw: Sam, a boy of seven with short black hair and a red shirt, sits up in bed with a startled face and hands near his ears; outside the window an old blue truck puffs a cartoon cloud of grey smoke.
scene:L1.01:0.why: Sam startled; the noise is a truck

scene:L1.01:1.text: Sam's little sister covered her ears and laughed. "That truck is louder than a drum," she said.
scene:L1.01:1.draw: Sam's little sister, a girl of four with two braids and a yellow dress, covers her ears with both hands and laughs. Sam, a boy with short black hair and red shirt, grins beside her.

scene:L1.01:2.text: Their mother peeked out the window and shook her head. "Every single morning," she sighed, but she was smiling.
scene:L1.01:2.draw: A mother with curly brown hair and a green cardigan peeks through a window curtain, shaking her head while smiling warmly. A hint of an old blue truck shows outside.
scene:L1.01:2.why: mother shakes head but smiles (amused and annoyed)

scene:L1.01:3.text: Outside, the truck coughed, sputtered, and finally started with a satisfying roar. Sam waved at the neighbor, who waved back, covered in oil and grinning proudly.
scene:L1.01:3.draw: An old blue truck roars with a little puff of cartoon smoke. A grey-bearded man in blue overalls, face smeared with oil, grins proudly. Sam, boy in red shirt, waves from the sidewalk.
scene:L1.01:3.why: neighbor fixing truck, oily and proud

scene:L1.02:0.text: Sam felt nervous walking into the new classroom. Everyone else already seemed to know each other, chatting and laughing near the window.
scene:L1.02:0.draw: Sam, a child with short black hair and a red shirt, stands nervously at a classroom door, hands clasped and worried eyes. Other children chat and laugh together near a sunny window.

scene:L1.02:1.text: Sam picked a desk near the back and sat down quietly, hoping nobody would notice how fast their heart was beating. Then a girl named Mia turned around and smiled.
scene:L1.02:1.draw: Sam, short black hair and red shirt, sits alone at a desk near the back, shoulders hunched, hand on chest. In front, Mia, a girl with curly dark hair and an orange sweater, turns and smiles.

scene:L1.02:2.text: "Are you new? I sat exactly where you are on my first day too," she said.
scene:L1.02:2.draw: Mia, a girl with curly dark hair and an orange sweater, leans over her chair and talks kindly to Sam, who has short black hair and a red shirt and looks surprised.

scene:L1.02:3.text: "It gets easier by lunchtime, I promise." Sam felt a small knot of worry loosen. Maybe today wouldn't be so bad after all.
scene:L1.02:3.draw: Sam, short black hair and red shirt, smiles with relief at a desk. Mia, curly dark hair and orange sweater, smiles beside him. Other children sit happily in the sunny classroom.

scene:L1.03:0.text: At the big race, cars zoom around the track faster than the eye can follow. But every few laps, a driver has to pull into a special lane called the pit.
scene:L1.03:0.draw: A red race car turns off the main track into a side lane while two other race cars continue side by side on the main track, a few cheering people in the stands
scene:L1.03:0.draw_v1: Colorful race cars zoom blurred around a curved track while one red car turns into a side lane. Spectators wave from the stands under a blue sky.

scene:L1.03:1.text: There, a whole team is waiting — not to rest, but to work at incredible speed. In under ten seconds, they can change all four tires, clean the windshield, and send the car roaring back onto the track.
scene:L1.03:1.draw: Four crew members in matching yellow suits swarm a red race car in the pit: one swaps each wheel while another wipes the windshield. The driver waits inside, helmet on.
scene:L1.03:1.why: team changing four tires and windshield fast

scene:L1.03:2.text: Everyone has one exact job, and they practice it over and over so nothing goes wrong when it really counts. A single second lost in the pit can cost a driver the whole race.
scene:L1.03:2.draw: A pit crew of four in yellow suits stands in a tidy line, each holding a different tool, ready and focused. A red race car waits in front of them in the pit lane.
scene:L1.03:2.why: each person has one exact job

scene:L1.04:0.text: Every Tuesday, a truck brings fresh bread to Mr. Iqbal's small shop before sunrise.
scene:L1.04:0.draw: A delivery truck stops at a small shop at dawn while a driver unloads baskets of fresh bread. An older man with a white moustache and brown vest stands in the doorway smiling.

scene:L1.04:1.text: He counts on it — his whole morning depends on those loaves being on the shelf before the first customers arrive. But this Tuesday, seven o'clock came and went, and the truck never appeared.
scene:L1.04:1.draw: Close view of Mr. Iqbal, an older man with a white moustache and brown vest, with big worried eyebrows raised in the middle and a worried frown, in front of his small shop with empty shelves behind him
scene:L1.04:1.draw_v1: Mr. Iqbal, an older man with a white moustache and brown vest, stands in front of his small shop with empty shelves behind him, looking worried, with a bright morning sky and no truck in sight.

scene:L1.04:2.text: Mr. Iqbal called the bakery three times, growing more frustrated with each unanswered ring.
scene:L1.04:2.draw: Mr. Iqbal (white moustache, brown vest) holding an old corded telephone to his ear with a frustrated frown, one hand on his head, full head and hand with clear margin above, centered in a rounded panel, no cropping.
scene:L1.04:2.draw_v1: Mr. Iqbal, white moustache and brown vest, holds a telephone to his ear in his shop with a frowning, frustrated face, one hand on his head.

scene:L1.04:3.text: Finally, his daughter suggested checking the neighborhood group chat — and there it was: the delivery driver's van had a flat tire two streets away. Mr.
scene:L1.04:3.draw: A girl about ten with a ponytail and purple top shows a man in a blue shirt her phone; in the foreground a clearly readable white delivery van with a visibly flat front tyre (tyre squashed on the ground), no text or logos on the van, everything inside the frame with margin on the right.
scene:L1.04:3.draw_v1: A girl of ten with a ponytail and purple top shows a man in a blue shirt a phone; a white delivery van with a flat tyre stands beside them.

scene:L1.04:4.text: Iqbal grabbed his bicycle pump without a second thought and pedaled over to help.
scene:L1.04:4.draw: Mr. Iqbal, white moustache and brown vest, pedals an old bicycle carrying a long black bicycle pump clearly sticking out of the front basket, smiling with effort
scene:L1.04:4.draw_v1: Mr. Iqbal, white moustache and brown vest, pedals a bicycle down the street, a bicycle pump in his basket. Ahead, a delivery van with a flat tire waits.

scene:L1.05:0.text: When old Mrs. Chaudhry got too tired to walk her dog Bruno every morning, the neighbors worried he'd be stuck inside all day.
scene:L1.05:0.draw: Old woman with a white bun and lavender cardigan slumped tired in an armchair, eyes half closed; shaggy brown dog Bruno sitting by a door looking sadly back over his shoulder toward the door, a green leash held in his mouth, clear margin above the bun, rounded panel, no cropping.
scene:L1.05:0.why: Mrs. Chaudhry too tired; Bruno needs walks
scene:L1.05:0.draw_v1: Old Mrs. Chaudhry, a woman with a white bun and lavender cardigan, sits tired in an armchair. Bruno, a shaggy brown dog, looks sadly at the door with his leash in his mouth.

scene:L1.05:1.text: Instead, something wonderful happened: a rotation started. On Mondays, the twins next door took Bruno to the park.
scene:L1.05:1.draw: Two twin boys in matching blue caps walk Bruno, a shaggy brown dog, on a leash through a green park. Bruno trots happily with his tail up.

scene:L1.05:2.text: On Tuesdays, it was the teenager from the corner house, who said walking Bruno was the only exercise he actually enjoyed. By the weekend, half the street had a turn.
scene:L1.05:2.draw: A tall teenage boy in a green hoodie jogs along a path with Bruno, a shaggy brown dog, running happily beside him. Both look joyful and active.

scene:L1.05:3.text: Bruno, delighted, seemed to know exactly whose door to wait outside each morning, tail thumping the second the right person stepped out.
scene:L1.05:3.draw: Shaggy brown dog Bruno sitting next to an open orange front door with its tail blurred from wagging; a smiling neighbor in a green hoodie stepping out of the doorway holding a leash, full heads with clear margin above, rounded panel, no cropping.
scene:L1.05:3.draw_v1: Bruno, a shaggy brown dog, sits waiting at a front door with his tail blurred from wagging. A neighbor in a green hoodie steps out smiling and holds a leash.

scene:L1.06:0.text: In everyday English, if someone says a person "got the sack," they don't mean an actual bag — they mean the person lost their job. Nobody agrees exactly where the phrase came from, but one popular idea goes back hundreds of years, when tradesmen carried their own tools to work in a sack.
scene:L1.06:0.draw: A smiling man in a suit points at a burlap sack on a table, with a thought bubble showing a worker packing hammers and saws into it. A cartoon question mark floats above.
scene:L1.06:0.why: sack of tools idea behind the phrase

scene:L1.06:1.text: If you were let go, you packed up your sack of tools and left — hence "getting the sack." Whether or not that story is completely accurate, the phrase has stuck around for so long that most English speakers use it without ever thinking about actual sacks at all.
scene:L1.06:1.draw: An old-time craftsman in a flat cap walks away from a workshop carrying a burlap sack of hammers and saws over his shoulder, looking sad. A boss stands in the doorway.
scene:L1.06:1.why: let go, leaves with sack of tools

scene:L1.07:0.text: On busy construction sites, supervisors learned something surprising: workers who took one proper ten-minute break mid-morning, every single day at the same time, made fewer mistakes in the afternoon than workers who pushed through without stopping. It seemed backwards at first — how could stopping work make people more productive?
scene:L1.07:0.draw: Four construction workers in yellow hard hats sit together on a bench in the shade at mid-morning, resting. Behind them stands an unfinished brick building with a crane.

scene:L1.07:1.text: But the body and brain both need small pauses to reset concentration, especially doing careful, repetitive tasks in the heat. Now some companies build the "ten o'clock rule" right into the schedule: everyone stops together, drinks water, and stretches — no exceptions, not even for the boss.
scene:L1.07:1.draw: Construction workers in hard hats, including one in a white hat, drink water from bottles and stretch their arms together on a building site. Everyone including the boss is stopped, smiling.

scene:L1.08:0.text: Before smartphones and ride-share apps existed, neighbors organized a shared morning school run with nothing more than a notebook taped inside someone's kitchen cabinet. Every family wrote down which mornings they could take the children, and everyone else simply trusted the schedule.
scene:L1.08:0.draw: A kitchen cabinet door is open with a plain notebook taped inside. A parent in an apron points at it while two children with backpacks wait by the door.

scene:L1.08:1.text: It sounds old-fashioned, but the system worked because everyone had something to lose if they broke the trust — miss your turn, and you'd better believe your neighbors would remember. These days, apps handle the scheduling, but the core idea hasn't changed at all: a group of people agreeing to share both the effort and the waiting, so no single person carries the whole burden alone.
scene:L1.08:1.draw: Draw the left adult with a clear face: two eyes, a small smile, and visible hair, same style as the other characters.
scene:L1.08:1.why: neighbors trust and share school run
scene:L1.08:1.draw_v1: Several neighbors stand in a sunny street shaking hands, children waving from the back seat of a family car. One parent holds a smartphone and another holds a notebook.

scene:L1.09:0.text: When a stranger's bag turns up with no name on it, most people feel a small pull in two directions at once — curiosity about what's inside, and a clear sense that opening it isn't quite right. Workplaces that handle a lot of lost property usually have a simple rule for this: log it, store it somewhere safe, and hold it for a set number of days before deciding what happens next.
scene:L1.09:0.draw: A woman looks at a plain brown bag on a bench with a curious face, one hand reaching and the other hand holding it back. A small thought bubble shows a question mark.

scene:L1.09:1.text: It sounds almost too basic to matter, but that small bit of structure is exactly what stops an honest mistake from turning into an argument later about who touched what, and when.
scene:L1.09:1.draw: A friendly clerk in a blue vest places a brown bag onto a tidy shelf, other plain bags sit neatly on the shelves.

scene:L1.10:0.text: English is full of words that look and sound exactly the same but mean completely different things depending on how they're used — linguists call these homonyms. "Well" can mean a deep hole dug for water, or it can mean feeling healthy, or it can mean "okay, so..." at the start of a sentence.
scene:L1.10:0.draw: A smiling child with one fist raised and thumb clearly pointing up, beside the stone well with bucket; a person with a clear, solid thought bubble.
scene:L1.10:0.draw_v1: Three small panels in one picture: a deep stone well with a bucket, a smiling healthy child giving a thumbs up, and a person starting to speak with a thought bubble.

scene:L1.10:1.text: "Bill" can be a person's name, a piece of paper telling you what you owe, or the beak of a bird. Context — the words around a word — is what tells a listener or reader which meaning is meant.
scene:L1.10:1.draw: Three objects in a row: a smiling boy in a green shirt waving, a paper receipt held by a hand, and a bird with a big orange beak.
scene:L1.10:1.why: three meanings of bill: name, paper, beak

scene:L1.10:2.text: This is exactly why understanding a whole sentence matters so much more than knowing single words in isolation.
scene:L1.10:2.draw: A girl sits reading a book with a glowing light bulb above her head, with a small bird and a well drawn around her. She looks happy and clever.

scene:L1.11:0.text: The word "vet" hides a small trap: most people think first of an animal doctor, but "vet" is also short for "veteran" — someone who has served in the military — and it's a verb too, as in "the company vetted every new driver before hiring them," meaning they checked the person's background carefully. Three different meanings, one small word, and only the sentence around it tells you which one is meant.
scene:L1.11:0.draw: A friendly vet in a white coat with a stethoscope checking a golden dog; one single scene only
scene:L1.11:0.draw_v1: Three small panels in one picture: a friendly vet checking a dog, a veteran in uniform with a medal saluting, and a manager checking a driver's papers with a magnifying glass.

scene:L1.11:1.text: Careful readers learn to slow down for a half-second whenever a short, familiar-looking word suddenly doesn't quite fit the sentence — that pause is often the first sign a word is doing a job you didn't expect.
scene:L1.11:1.draw: A girl with glasses pauses with a finger on a page, one eyebrow raised and a thoughtful face, with a small question mark above her head.

scene:L1.12:0.text: Every single letter of the English alphabet has now had its own proper introduction — some of them, like c and k, even share a job. It took twelve lessons to get here, on purpose: rushing through all 26 letters in a week or two sounds efficient, but it means most of them never get practiced enough to become automatic.
scene:L1.12:0.draw: A smiling child stands on top of a short staircase of plain wooden steps, waving happily, with a row of plain colourful building blocks with no marks on them beside the stairs.
scene:L1.12:0.why: all letters reached after twelve steps

scene:L1.12:1.text: From here, nothing new needs to be "discovered" — the next lessons are about combining these same 26 letters in cleverer and cleverer ways: two letters making one sound, sounds joining into longer words, and patterns repeating across hundreds of different words once you know what to look for.
scene:L1.12:1.draw: A child at a table joins colorful puzzle pieces into longer chains, proud and curious. Some pieces snap together in pairs while others make a bigger pattern.

scene:L1.13:0.text: In busy warehouses, a single misread letter on a shipping label can send a package hundreds of miles in the wrong direction. That's why professional warehouse workers are trained to read labels a specific, careful way: never glance quickly at a whole word and guess, but check the exact letters, especially any that could be confused with another — b and d, or the number 0 and the letter O.
scene:L1.13:0.draw: A busy warehouse worker with a frown holds a shipping box and studies it carefully; one big delivery truck beside him clearly pointing the wrong way
scene:L1.13:0.why: careful checking of labels avoids wrong destination
scene:L1.13:0.draw_v1: A busy warehouse worker with a frown holds a shipping box and studies it carefully, a delivery truck parked in the background pointing the wrong way.

scene:L1.13:1.text: Some warehouses even print certain confusable letters in a special typeface designed to make them look as different from each other as possible. It's a small design choice built entirely around a very human, very ordinary reading mistake.
scene:L1.13:1.draw: A smiling worker holds a box close to his eyes with a magnifying glass, checking one marking carefully, while shelves of tidy boxes stand behind him.

scene:L1.14:0.text: Fourteen lessons ago, this course started with three sounds and a handful of made-up "alien words." Today's check uses every single letter in English, a spelling rule, a plural ending, and twenty-four words that don't even follow the normal rules — and asks for all of it back, cold, without any warm-up hints. That's not a small ask.
scene:L1.14:0.draw: A girl at a desk with a big blank test paper, a thoughtful focused face with a small smile, pencil in hand
scene:L1.14:0.draw_v1: A child sits at a desk looking at a big test paper with a determined face, with a long path of fourteen stepping stones behind her leading back to a tiny starting point.

scene:L1.14:1.text: Whatever the score turns out to be, getting through fourteen full lessons of new material, in order, each one building on the last, is real, durable progress — the kind that doesn't disappear the way a memorized page would. What comes next, in Level 2, isn't starting over; it's the exact same skill, aimed at bigger and bigger words.
scene:L1.14:1.draw: A proud child stands on top of a hill of fourteen stone steps, arms raised, with a bigger hill and a path leading upward ahead. She smiles and the sun shines.

scene:L2.01:0.text: A fisherman named Tom worked on a small boat every morning. One day, Tom caught a fish that was absolutely **enormous** — far bigger than any fish he had ever seen before.
scene:L2.01:0.draw: A fisherman named Tom, a man with a gray beard and yellow raincoat, stands in a small boat holding a huge silver fish, eyes wide. The fish is bigger than his body.

scene:L2.01:1.text: It was so large that he could barely lift it into the boat! Tom's friends at the harbor could not believe their eyes.
scene:L2.01:1.draw: Tom, a man with a gray beard and yellow raincoat, struggles to lift an enormous silver fish into his boat. On the harbor, friends with astonished faces point.

scene:L2.01:2.text: "That fish is enormous!" they shouted. Tom laughed and said an enormous fish like that would feed the whole street for a week.
scene:L2.01:2.draw: Tom, gray beard and yellow raincoat, laughs next to an enormous silver fish while three friends on the dock shout with open mouths and raised hands.

scene:L2.01:3.text: He shared it with every family on his road, and everyone had a wonderful dinner that night.
scene:L2.01:3.draw: Tom, gray beard and yellow raincoat, gives pieces of an enormous fish to smiling families standing at their doors along a small street. Each family holds a plate.

scene:L2.02:0.text: A little cat named Pip was very **curious**. Every single day, Pip wanted to know what was happening on the other side of the garden wall.
scene:L2.02:0.draw: Pip the small orange cat with white paws sits on a garden path, head tilted up, eyes looking up at a tall brick wall, ears forward; full wall inside frame with margin on all sides, flat vector, soft rounded shapes, no outlines
scene:L2.02:0.draw_v1: Pip, a small orange cat with white paws, sits on a garden path staring up at a tall brick wall, ears pointed forward with a curious look.

scene:L2.02:1.text: One afternoon, Pip's curious nose led her straight into a bush, where she found a family of hedgehogs curled up asleep! Pip was so curious that she gently poked one with her paw.
scene:L2.02:1.draw: Pip the orange cat with white paws leans forward and gently taps a curled sleeping hedgehog with one paw, the hedgehog's spines up in surprise
scene:L2.02:1.draw_v1: Pip, a small orange cat with white paws, pokes a paw gently at a curled-up sleepy hedgehog under a green bush. A few more hedgehogs sleep nearby.

scene:L2.02:2.text: The hedgehog woke up, uncurled, and gave a tiny, surprised squeak. Pip jumped back, but she was still curious — she sat and watched the hedgehogs for the rest of the afternoon, learning something new about her garden.
scene:L2.02:2.draw: Two-panel-in-one-image is not allowed; draw only the surprise moment: hedgehog standing up with a startled face, Pip the orange cat leaping back with wide eyes, both fully in frame
scene:L2.02:2.draw_v1: The hedgehog stands up with a surprised face as Pip, a small orange cat with white paws, leaps back with wide eyes. Later, Pip sits and watches calmly.

scene:L2.03:0.text: Grandpa was usually calm, but one afternoon he got absolutely **furious**. His favorite garden tools had gone missing from the shed, and he was sure someone had taken them without asking.
scene:L2.03:0.draw: Grandpa, an old man with white hair and a green sweater, looks angry in front of an open empty garden shed, fists clenched and a red face. Empty hooks hang inside.

scene:L2.03:1.text: He searched the whole yard, muttering to himself, getting more and more furious with every empty corner. Then his granddaughter walked out holding the tools.
scene:L2.03:1.draw: Same grandpa as the other scenes: old man with white hair, green sweater, angry face with fists up, searching the yard; granddaughter with black ponytail and pink shirt carrying garden tools in the background; flat vector, soft rounded shapes
scene:L2.03:1.draw_v1: Grandpa, white hair and green sweater, searches angrily around the yard with his fists up. In the background, his granddaughter, a girl with a black ponytail and pink shirt, carries garden tools.

scene:L2.03:2.text: "I borrowed them to fix my bike, Grandpa — I forgot to tell you!" she said. Grandpa's furious face softened into a small smile.
scene:L2.03:2.draw: Granddaughter with black ponytail and pink shirt holds a spade and rake and points at her small bike with a visibly broken dangling chain; grandpa with white hair and green sweater stands calmly beside her; flat vector, soft rounded shapes
scene:L2.03:2.why: she borrowed tools to fix bike
scene:L2.03:2.draw_v1: A girl with a black ponytail and pink shirt holds out a spade and a rake, pointing to her small bike with a broken chain. Grandpa, white hair and green sweater, looks calmer.

scene:L2.03:3.text: "Next time," he said, "just tell me first, and I won't have to get furious over nothing."
scene:L2.03:3.draw: Grandpa, white hair and green sweater, smiles gently and kneels to talk with his granddaughter, black ponytail and pink shirt. She holds the garden tools and smiles back.

scene:L2.04:0.text: Little Ana loved puzzles more than anything, but one rainy afternoon she found herself completely **puzzled**. Her grandmother had given her a box with no picture on the lid and no instructions inside — just three hundred loose pieces.
scene:L2.04:0.draw: Ana, a girl with a short black bob and a blue dress, sits on the floor looking confused at a plain empty box and many loose plain puzzle pieces; rain falls outside the window.

scene:L2.04:1.text: Ana sat there, puzzled, turning pieces over in her hands, unsure where to even begin. She tried the edges first, but she was still puzzled about which piece connected to which.
scene:L2.04:1.draw: Ana, girl with short black bob and blue dress, sits on a rug turning a puzzle piece with a confused frown; a small light thought bubble with a question mark floats above her head, separate from her hair; pieces spread on the rug; flat vector, soft rounded shapes
scene:L2.04:1.draw_v1: Ana, a girl with a short black bob and a blue dress, turns a puzzle piece in her hands with a confused frown and a question mark above her head. Pieces cover the rug.

scene:L2.04:2.text: Finally, her grandmother sat beside her and said, "When you are puzzled, start with the corners — there are only four, and they always fit first." Ana found a corner, then another, and slowly her puzzled frown turned into a grin.
scene:L2.04:2.draw: Ana's grandmother, a woman with gray hair and round glasses, sits beside Ana, a girl with a short black bob and blue dress, and points to a puzzle corner piece. Ana starts to grin.

scene:L2.05:0.text: After a full day at the farm, feeding the animals, mending fences, and carrying heavy buckets of water, farmer Iqbal was completely **exhausted**. His arms ached, his legs felt like stone, and he could barely climb the steps to his own porch.
scene:L2.05:0.draw: Farmer Iqbal, a tired man with a mustache and straw hat, carries two heavy water buckets near a fence, with a drooping posture and half-closed eyes. A cow stands nearby.

scene:L2.05:1.text: His son offered to finish the last chore, but Iqbal was too exhausted even to explain what needed doing — he just pointed and nodded. He sat down, closed his eyes, and within minutes he was fast asleep in his chair, still wearing his muddy boots.
scene:L2.05:1.draw: Farmer Iqbal, a mustached man with a straw hat, sits on a porch step too tired to speak and weakly points. His young son in a red cap stands ready beside him.

scene:L2.05:2.text: When he woke an hour later, he felt much better, though still a little exhausted, and very glad his son had taken care of the rest.
scene:L2.05:2.draw: Farmer Iqbal, a mustached man in a straw hat and muddy boots, sleeps in a chair on the porch with his hat over his eyes. His son in a red cap works in the yard.
scene:L2.05:2.why: asleep in chair with muddy boots

scene:L2.06:0.text: Before crossing the busy market road, Aunt Rukhsana was always very **cautious**. She would stop at the edge, look left, then right, then left again, even if the road looked completely empty.
scene:L2.06:0.draw: Aunt Rukhsana, a woman with a green sun hat and a purple dress, stands at the edge of a busy market road and carefully looks left, with a boy in a yellow shirt beside her.

scene:L2.06:1.text: Her nephew used to tease her about being so cautious, saying it took forever just to cross one small street. One evening, though, a bicycle came speeding around the corner at exactly the moment they stepped off the curb — and because Aunt Rukhsana had been cautious and was watching closely, she pulled her nephew back just in time.
scene:L2.06:1.draw: A bicycle zooms around a corner while Aunt Rukhsana, green sun hat and purple dress, pulls back her nephew, a boy in a yellow shirt, from the curb. Both look surprised.
scene:L2.06:1.why: she pulled nephew back just in time

scene:L2.06:2.text: After that, her nephew never teased her again. "Better cautious than sorry," she always says, and now he says it too.
scene:L2.06:2.draw: Aunt Rukhsana, green sun hat and purple dress, smiles kindly beside her nephew, a boy in a yellow shirt, who nods and smiles back. They stand safely at the edge of the street.

scene:L2.07:0.text: When the school bake sale raised more money than anyone expected, the head teacher decided to give every extra rupee to the small clinic down the road. She was **grateful** — truly grateful — for how hard the students had worked, baking and selling from early morning until the last plate was empty.
scene:L2.07:0.draw: A head teacher, a woman with short gray hair and a navy jacket, smiles with misty happy eyes at a school bake sale table covered in empty plates. Children in aprons cheer around her.

scene:L2.07:1.text: One student asked why she looked close to tears. "I am just so grateful," she said.
scene:L2.07:1.draw: A young student in an apron looks up at the teacher, a woman with short gray hair and a navy jacket, who has teary happy eyes and a hand on her chest. Empty baking trays are behind them.

scene:L2.07:2.text: "You worked all day, and now families who could not afford medicine will get help." The students felt proud too, and decided that being the reason someone else got help was better than any prize. They planned an even bigger, more grateful bake sale for next year.
scene:L2.07:2.draw: The teacher with short gray hair and navy jacket hands a jar of coins to a smiling nurse at a small clinic door, while proud children in aprons stand behind her.

scene:L2.08:0.text: A young dog named Bruno was usually eager to try anything new, but the first time his owner brought out a bicycle, Bruno was strangely **reluctant**. He backed away, tail low, refusing to go anywhere near the strange spinning wheels.
scene:L2.08:0.draw: Bruno, a young brown dog with floppy ears, backs away from a bicycle with a low tail and worried eyes. His owner, a girl in a red jacket, holds a leash and watches him.

scene:L2.08:1.text: His owner tried treats, gentle words, even a favorite toy — but Bruno stayed reluctant, watching from a safe distance. Then one afternoon, the owner simply sat beside the bicycle and let Bruno sniff it in his own time, with no pushing at all.
scene:L2.08:1.draw: Bruno, a shaggy brown dog (clearly a dog), sits shyly far on the right looking away, while a girl smiles at him from the left
scene:L2.08:1.draw_v1: A girl in a red jacket holds out a dog treat and a toy toward Bruno, a young brown dog who sits far away, tail low, near a bicycle. He looks away shyly.

scene:L2.08:2.text: Slowly, Bruno's reluctant ears perked up, and he stepped closer. By the end of the week, the once-reluctant Bruno was trotting happily alongside the bicycle on every walk.
scene:L2.08:2.draw: Bruno, a young brown dog with floppy ears, trots happily beside a bicycle on a park path, tail wagging. A girl in a red jacket rides smiling beside him.

scene:L2.09:0.text: When the class hamster went missing from its cage on a Friday afternoon, every student was **delighted** to hear it had been found safe behind the bookshelf on Monday morning. The teacher was delighted too, and let the whole class take turns holding it gently, one by one.
scene:L2.09:0.draw: A teacher with a green scarf holds a small hamster gently while smiling, and happy children in a classroom gather around. A bookshelf stands behind them.

scene:L2.09:1.text: One boy, who had been especially worried all weekend, was so delighted that he asked if he could bring the hamster home just for one night, to make sure it was really okay. His teacher smiled at how delighted — and relieved — he looked, and said yes, as long as his parents agreed.
scene:L2.09:1.draw: A boy in a blue sweater, delighted, holds a small hamster in his hands and looks up at his smiling teacher in a green scarf. A cage sits on a table.

scene:L2.09:2.text: That evening, the whole family took turns being delighted by the tiny hamster running on its wheel.
scene:L2.09:2.draw: A family of four, mother, father, boy in blue sweater, and a small girl, laugh together around a small cage where a hamster runs on its wheel. Everyone looks delighted.

scene:L2.10:0.text: Uncle Hamid had asked his nephew, Bilal, to water the plants every single day while he was away — just that one job. When Hamid came home a week later and found every plant wilted and brown, he was **stubborn** about not letting it go.
scene:L2.10:0.draw: Uncle Hamid, a man with a gray beard and brown vest, frowns with crossed arms in front of a garden full of dry, brown wilted plants. A suitcase is at his feet.

scene:L2.10:1.text: "It's just water, once a day," he said, again and again, refusing to accept Bilal's excuses about being busy with exams. Bilal, just as stubborn, insisted exams mattered more than plants.
scene:L2.10:1.draw: Uncle Hamid, gray beard and brown vest, and his nephew Bilal, a teenage boy with curly hair and a gray hoodie, stand face to face with crossed arms, both frowning and refusing to listen.

scene:L2.10:2.text: Neither would budge for two whole days. Finally, Hamid's wife stepped in and pointed out that both of them were being equally stubborn over something they could fix together in ten minutes.
scene:L2.10:2.draw: Hamid's wife, a woman with a red cardigan, stands between Uncle Hamid with gray beard and brown vest, and Bilal with curly hair and gray hoodie, who both look away with crossed arms. She raises a calming hand.

scene:L2.10:3.text: They laughed, apologized, and replanted the garden side by side that weekend.
scene:L2.10:3.draw: Uncle Hamid with gray beard and Bilal with curly hair and gray hoodie laugh together while planting new green seedlings in the garden. Hamid's wife in a red cardigan watches smiling.

scene:L2.11:0.text: The night before her first big exam, Ayesha felt more **anxious** than she had ever felt before. Her stomach fluttered, her hands felt cold, and she kept checking the clock, worried she was somehow forgetting something important.
scene:L2.11:0.draw: Ayesha, a girl of twelve with long black hair and a yellow pajama top, sits on her bed at night looking worried with hands on her tummy; moonlight shines through the window.

scene:L2.11:1.text: Her older sister noticed how anxious she looked and sat down beside her. "Being a little anxious means you care," her sister said, "but let's make a short plan so the anxious feeling has less to hold onto." Together they wrote down exactly what Ayesha needed for the morning, checked it twice, and set two alarms.
scene:L2.11:1.draw: Ayesha, a girl with long black hair and yellow pajama top, sits on a bed beside her older sister, who has short curly hair and a purple shirt and holds a pencil and a drawn checklist.

scene:L2.11:2.text: Ayesha still felt a bit anxious as she fell asleep, but far less than before — and in the morning, she walked into the exam room calm and ready.
scene:L2.11:2.draw: Ayesha, a girl of twelve with long black hair, walks into a bright classroom from the right with a pencil in her hand, the whole room inside the frame with a few desks
scene:L2.11:2.draw_v1: Ayesha, a girl with long black hair, walks calmly and confidently into a bright exam room at dawn with a pencil in hand, smiling slightly. Rows of desks are ahead.

scene:L2.12:0.text: A wealthy trader in the old bazaar was known across the whole street for being unusually **generous**. Every evening, before he closed his stall, he would give away whatever fruit and bread had not sold that day — never selling it cheap at the last minute, always simply giving it to whoever needed it most.
scene:L2.12:0.draw: Pull the composition back so the stall counter, baskets and all people sit fully inside the frame with a margin on every side. The bald trader in a gold vest holds out fruit and bread baskets to smiling people under lanterns in an evening bazaar.
scene:L2.12:0.draw_v1: A wealthy trader, a bald man with a round belly and a gold vest, hands baskets of fruit and bread to smiling people at his bazaar stall in the evening.

scene:L2.12:1.text: His neighbors thought he must be losing money, but the trader just smiled and said being generous had brought him more good luck and more loyal customers than any clever deal ever had. One winter, when his own stall caught fire, every single family he had once helped showed up the next morning with tools, wood, and cash to help him rebuild — proof, he said, that generous kindness always finds its way back.
scene:L2.12:1.draw: A rebuilt wooden market stall in warm orange wood, a hammer lying on the counter and a small coin purse beside it, a happy stall owner standing behind
scene:L2.12:1.draw_v1: Neighbors of different ages arrive carrying wood planks, tools, and a coin purse to a rebuilt market stall, where the bald trader in a gold vest smiles gratefully. A blackened old stall frame stands nearby.

scene:L2.13:0.text: Retrieval passage: A stubborn old goat named Bella refused to leave the muddy field even when it started to rain hard. Her owner, cautious as always, did not want to drag a furious, wet goat across a slippery yard, so he waited, patient, under the barn roof.
scene:L2.13:0.draw: Bella the stubborn brown goat with floppy ears stands in a muddy rainy field with eyes shut and head up, refusing to move. Visible rain streaks fall around her. An adult man in a yellow raincoat waits patiently under the barn roof, a few steps away.
scene:L2.13:0.why: goat stubborn in rain, owner cautious
scene:L2.13:0.draw_v1: Bella, a stubborn brown goat with floppy ears, stands in a muddy rainy field with eyes shut and head up, refusing to move. Her owner, a man in a yellow raincoat, waits patiently under a barn roof.

scene:L2.13:1.text: After an hour of stubborn standing in the rain, Bella finally got cold enough to trot inside on her own — no longer stubborn, just cautious about getting even wetter. Her owner laughed, dried her off, and said a stubborn goat always changes its mind eventually, as long as you stay cautious and let it happen in its own time.
scene:L2.13:1.draw: Bella, a shivering brown goat, trots into a barn while the owner in a yellow raincoat laughs and dries her with a big towel. Rain falls outside.
scene:L2.13:1.why: goat comes inside, owner dries her

scene:L3.01:0.text: A long time ago, people who wanted to send a message far away used pigeons. A trained pigeon could find its way home from a hundred miles off.
scene:L3.01:0.draw: A solid white pigeon with a clear outline-free flat-vector body, fully inside the frame with top margin, flying over green hills and a winding road. A small rolled paper message is tied to its leg with a thin string. A small farmhouse sits in the distance. Same soft rounded flat-vector style as the rest of the sheet.
scene:L3.01:0.draw_v1: A white pigeon flies over green hills and a winding road carrying a tiny rolled message tied to its leg. A small farmhouse is in the distance.

scene:L3.01:1.text: Today we call sending a fast, important message 'urgent' — it means it cannot wait.
scene:L3.01:1.draw: A messenger in a red cap runs very fast along a road holding a rolled message, with a pigeon flying above. Dust clouds puff behind him as he hurries.

scene:L3.02:0.text: Before bikes had rubber tires, riders used wheels with iron rims. Every bump in the road shook the whole bike — people called it a 'bone-shaker.' A ride that should have felt smooth instead felt rough and tiring.
scene:L3.02:0.draw: A man in an old-fashioned hat rides a wooden bicycle with iron wheels over a bumpy cobbled road, his body shaking and eyes squeezed shut. Little bounce lines show the rough ride.

scene:L3.03:0.text: Mules are often used on farms because they are known to be very sturdy. A mule can carry a heavy load over rough ground for a long time without tiring, which makes it a reliable partner for farm work.
scene:L3.03:0.draw: A strong brown mule carries a big load of sacks across a stony hillside, with a farmer in a straw hat walking beside it and smiling. The mule walks steadily.

scene:L3.04:0.text: A shopkeeper's closing routine matters because a rushed close can leave a door unlocked or cash uncounted. A careful routine, done the same way every night, reduces the chance of a costly mistake.
scene:L3.04:0.draw: A shopkeeper, a woman in a blue apron, turns a key in her shop door at night, with a moon above and coins neatly stacked on a counter behind her. She looks careful and calm.

scene:L3.05:0.text: Engineers who design robots must consider every possible task the machine will face, because a robot cannot adapt on its own the way a person can. A well-designed robot follows a precise set of instructions, and even a small gap in those instructions can cause a big mistake.
scene:L3.05:0.draw: A friendly engineer with glasses and a white coat points at a small round robot holding a tool, with a thoughtful frown. The robot stands still at a tidy workbench.

scene:L3.06:0.text: A customer who takes the time to leave a kind note is showing genuine gratitude — a real, felt thanks, not just a quick 'thanks' said out of habit. Genuine gratitude tends to stick with a person much longer than a routine thank-you.
scene:L3.06:0.draw: A smiling customer in a green jacket hands a folded paper note with a drawn heart to a shop worker in an apron, who looks touched and happy. A counter separates them.

scene:L3.07:0.text: Engineers who inspect a bridge look for tiny cracks long before the bridge is actually in danger of failing. Catching a problem early, while it is still minor, is far cheaper and safer than waiting until it becomes a crisis.
scene:L3.07:0.draw: An engineer in a yellow helmet kneels on a bridge and points a flashlight at a tiny crack in the concrete, while another engineer with a clipboard watches closely.

scene:L3.08:0.text: Farmers markets let shoppers buy food directly from the people who grew it, which often means the produce is fresher than what has traveled a long distance to a big store. Buying this way also supports the local economy.
scene:L3.08:0.draw: A farmer in a straw hat hands a basket of fresh tomatoes and carrots to a smiling shopper at an outdoor market stall. Colorful vegetables fill the stall.

scene:L3.09:0.text: Before horses could be domesticated for riding, humans had to build a relationship of trust with an animal that is naturally alert to danger. A horse that trusts its rider will respond calmly even in a busy, noisy place.
scene:L3.09:0.draw: Close-up of a calm brown horse standing still in a yard, a girl in a red jacket beside its head with her hand gently stroking its neck, the horse's eyes half closed, no saddle or riding pose, flat vector, soft rounded shapes, no text.
scene:L3.09:0.draw_v1: A girl in a red jacket gently strokes the neck of a calm brown horse she is riding in a busy yard, with people and other animals around. The horse stands relaxed and trusting.

scene:L3.10:0.text: When trains are delayed during heavy rain, it is often because water can seep into the electrical system that controls the tracks, forcing a temporary shutdown until it is safe again.
scene:L3.10:0.draw: A train stands still on rainy tracks under dark clouds. A worker in a yellow raincoat looks at a wet signal box with a puddle, while passengers wait under umbrellas.
scene:L3.10:0.why: train stopped due to rain water

scene:L3.11:0.text: Communities that organize regular street clean-ups tend to build a stronger sense of civic pride, because neighbors who work side by side start to feel a shared responsibility for the place they live.
scene:L3.11:0.draw: Neighbors of different ages in green gloves pick up litter on a street with bags and brooms, smiling and working together. A tidy sunny neighborhood is behind them.

scene:L3.12:0.text: Traffic engineers study patterns in road congestion to figure out which streets need a second lane or a new signal. A small change, like a longer green light, can noticeably ease a slow commute for thousands of people.
scene:L3.12:0.draw: A busy road with many cars waiting at a traffic light, then a second lane with cars flowing, and a traffic engineer in an orange vest pointing at a green traffic light.

scene:L3.13:0.text: Talking through a big decision with someone you trust often reveals a perspective you had not considered on your own. A friend can point out a risk or an option you were too close to the problem to notice.
scene:L3.13:0.draw: Two friends on a park bench; the girl points at a thought bubble showing a forked road with a clear left path and a right path, each with a small simple icon, flat vector, soft rounded shapes, no text or letters.
scene:L3.13:0.draw_v1: Two friends sit on a park bench talking: a boy with glasses and a blue sweater with a hand on his chin, and a girl with curly hair pointing at a thought bubble showing two paths.

scene:L3.14:0.text: Choosing an outfit for an important meeting is about more than looking neat — it can genuinely affect how confident a person feels walking into the room, which in turn can affect how well they perform.
scene:L3.14:0.draw: A man in a neat blue suit stands confidently in front of a mirror adjusting his tie and smiling, a briefcase at his feet. A meeting room door is behind him.

scene:L3.15:0.text: Reading fiction before bed has been shown to help some people unwind, because following a story shifts attention away from the day's worries and toward a different, absorbing world.
scene:L3.15:0.draw: A woman in pajamas sits in bed reading a book, smiling dreamily, with a lamp glowing and a small moon outside the window. Dream clouds with castles float above her.

scene:L3.16:0.text: When a whole industry changes quickly, many workers must adapt by learning a new skill, which can feel daunting at first but often opens up options a person had not considered before.
scene:L3.16:0.draw: Two human characters at a desk: a young worker in an orange shirt, eyes wide and a nervous tight smile, staring at a big laptop; a friendly coworker in a green shirt pats his shoulder. Full figures with margin on all sides, flat vector, soft rounded shapes, no text.
scene:L3.16:0.draw_v1: A worker in an orange shirt looks at a big laptop with wide eyes and a nervous smile, a friendly coworker pats his shoulder encouragingly.

scene:L3.17:0.text: People often find that a day spent helping others, even a small task like a neighborhood clean-up, brings a deeper sense of satisfaction than a day spent purely on entertainment. Researchers call this the difference between pleasure and genuine fulfillment.
scene:L3.17:0.draw: Two volunteers in green shirts picking up litter on a grassy park with trees, one holding a full trash bag, both smiling and a little tired, no couch, no TV, no indoor furniture, flat vector, soft rounded shapes, no text.
scene:L3.17:0.draw_v1: Two volunteers in green shirts pick up litter in a park, smiling and tired, with a full bag. Nearby on a couch, a cartoon TV shows a person laughing, small and distant.

scene:L4.01:0.text: Long ago, before streetlights, farmers and travelers used the stars to find their way home. A bright, easy-to-spot group of stars is called a constellation.
scene:L4.01:0.draw: A farmer with a straw hat walks along a dark country path under a sky full of bright stars, with a glowing group of stars connected in a shape above. A small house with a lit window is ahead.

scene:L4.02:0.text: Long before cars, people used horses to travel. A caravan was a group of travelers — often with camels or horses — who journeyed together across long, hard roads for safety.
scene:L4.02:0.draw: A caravan of four camels and two horses walks together with travelers wrapped in scarves along a long sandy road at sunset. The group stays close together.

scene:L4.03:0.text: People who care for the sick and injured, easing pain and helping bodies heal, often say the work feels like a calling — something they feel deeply pulled to do, not just a job.
scene:L4.03:0.draw: A nurse in a light blue uniform gently bandages the arm of a child sitting on a bed, both smiling softly. A warm glow of light fills the clinic room.

scene:L4.04:0.text: In many places, wild animals like deer must be cautious around people, even kind ones, because their bodies are built to sense danger first and think later.
scene:L4.04:0.draw: A young deer with big ears stands alert at the edge of a green forest, looking toward a kind smiling woman who holds out her open empty hands from far away.
scene:L4.04:0.why: deer cautious even of kind people

scene:L4.05:0.text: When people work well together and things go smoothly, we sometimes say the day felt harmonious — everything and everyone fitting together without friction.
scene:L4.05:0.draw: A group of friends of different ages carry a picnic and play together in a sunny park, smiling and moving in harmony, with a big shared blanket in the middle.

scene:L4.06:0.text: When many strangers stay calm together during a problem, like a power cut or a delay, we can say the group showed resilience — the ability to handle a hard moment without falling apart.
scene:L4.06:0.draw: Dim station interior with most lamps switched off, a few warm lanterns glowing, a dark ceiling; a staff member in uniform holds one lantern up while families sit calmly together on benches, smiling and talking.
scene:L4.06:0.draw_v1: Many people of different ages stand in a train station while the lights flicker off, but they sit down calmly, talk, and smile at each other. A staff member holds a lantern.

scene:L4.07:0.text: In a busy public space, staff are trained to stay composed — calm and in control of their actions and voice — even when something unexpected happens, because panic spreads fast in a crowd.
scene:L4.07:0.draw: A station worker in an orange vest stands calmly with open hands in the middle of a crowded hall, smiling and speaking in a steady way. People around him look relaxed.

scene:L4.08:0.text: When someone stays calm and keeps making good choices even after something goes wrong, we can say they showed composure — a steady, level-headed response instead of panic.
scene:L4.08:0.draw: Girl sitting on a curb beside her light blue bicycle, a clearly visible white bandage wrapped on one knee, eyes looking down at the bike, taking a slow deep breath with a thoughtful expression; a round green bicycle helmet placed clearly next to her on the curb.
scene:L4.08:0.why: stays calm and makes good choices
scene:L4.08:0.draw_v1: A girl with a bandaged knee sits calmly on a curb next to her bicycle, taking a deep breath and looking at it with a thoughtful face. Her helmet is beside her.

scene:L4.09:0.text: A doctor or nurse who stays warm and patient with every person they see, even on an exhausting day, shows real compassion — caring about someone else's pain as if it were your own.
scene:L4.09:0.draw: A tired doctor in a white coat with dark circles under her eyes kneels warmly beside a sick child on a bed, smiling gently and holding the child's hand.
scene:L4.09:0.why: stays warm and patient while tired

scene:L4.10:0.text: A worker who checks their own work carefully before calling a job finished shows diligence — steady, careful effort, even on small details other people might not notice.
scene:L4.10:0.draw: A repair worker in blue overalls kneels beside a fixed sink and checks the pipes carefully with a flashlight and wrench, with a satisfied look. A neat toolbox is open beside him.

scene:L4.11:0.text: A good doctor, teacher, or guide often shows attentiveness — noticing small details about a person or a situation that someone in a hurry might miss.
scene:L4.11:0.draw: A kind teacher with glasses kneels beside a small child at a low table, looking closely at the child's drawing on paper with a small smile; other children draw at nearby tables in a bright classroom background. Flat vector, soft rounded shapes, no outlines, no text.
scene:L4.11:0.draw_v1: A kind teacher with glasses kneels beside a small child and looks closely at the child's drawing, noticing a tiny detail with a small smile. Other children draw in the background.

scene:L4.12:0.text: Some people believe small signs from nature — a bird building a nest, a certain season's first rain — carry meaning. Scientists call this kind of belief folklore: traditional stories and beliefs passed down between people, not proven by evidence but often carrying real wisdom about nature.
scene:L4.12:0.draw: A bird builds a nest in a leafy tree on a spring day, and below, an old woman with a gray shawl smiles and looks up, with first raindrops falling on her upturned hand.

scene:L4.13:0.text: People who keep working toward a goal, even slowly and through setbacks, show perseverance — refusing to give up, even when progress feels slow.
scene:L4.13:0.draw: A girl in a blue shirt climbs slowly up a steep grassy hill with a heavy backpack, sweating but smiling and determined; one small tree stands at the very top.

scene:L4.14:0.text: When someone works through a problem methodically instead of guessing, checking each possible cause one at a time, we call that troubleshooting — a careful, step-by-step way of finding and fixing what's wrong.
scene:L4.14:0.draw: A man in a blue shirt kneels next to a broken lamp, checking the plug with a small screwdriver, with a checklist drawn as little pictures nearby. He looks calm and patient.

scene:L4.15:0.text: A notice, a recipe, and a news report are three examples of functional text — writing whose main job is to help you do something (know when the water's off, cook a meal, understand a local event) rather than to tell a story.
scene:L4.15:0.draw: A smiling woman holds a small plain card in one hand, a pot steams on a nearby stove, she looks pleased and curious.
